note: Written by hand from the test runs; each shown finding is held by a strict xfail named in 'test'. Cited findings of sister cards are listed under 'cited' and are not filed again.

findings.claim: A torn last line (a write cut short) is reported as tampering: 'invalid JSON' and 'events dropped, a day file deleted, or the chain rewritten'; nothing names it a write cut short.
findings.expected: D-127: a torn last line is damage the next writer repairs, not an attack; the person reading the check must be told which it is.
findings.happened: tamper.json case torn_last_line: both verifiers fail with invalid JSON and the HEAD.json 'events dropped' message; after the next write the chain verifies (case torn_then_written).

findings.claim: make audit-verify without ANCHOR (tools/audit_verify.py without --heads) prints PASS on a fully re-chained forgery, a prefix, a fresh chain and a rollback, and says nothing about the signed heads it did not read.
findings.expected: D-355: only the signed heads catch a chain rewritten with its HEAD.json; the console says so when no anchor folder is set (audit.verify.no_anchor), the tool should too.
findings.happened: tamper.json: cli_no_heads_ok is PASS for rechained_with_head, prefix_with_head, fresh_chain_from_genesis and rollback_to_backup, with no note.

findings.claim: The steward's typed reason for a data-ops decision (page and /api/v1) reaches the audit chain in clear: a chart number, a name, a phone and an e-mail typed there are all stored as typed, in a store that is never erased.
findings.expected: D-272 (CR-016): no chart number in clear in the audit; writers pass free text through mask_ids/mask_detail.
findings.happened: POST /data-ops/batches/{bid}/decide and POST /api/v1/data/batches/{bid}/decide: the dataops.decide event's detail.reason holds all four planted values (routes.json, driven rows, leaks).

findings.claim: POST /ops/users (add) makes the account before its audit event; with the audit write failing (AuditFull) the request fails but the account stays, with no event. Reset (app.py:1293), scope (app.py:1308) and disable (app.py:1321) have the same order by reading.
findings.expected: The 13:30 rule: an audit trail that can be wrong is High; D-273 (DI-5) writes the event inside the change's transaction for marks and opt-outs. V3-18 found the same order for break-glass and five account-factor routes; this extends it to account creation.
findings.happened: With TB_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_MB set huge: 500, no console.user event, and users.get('atfull') returns the new account.

cited.what: the break-glass opening note reaches the audit in clear; seen again here (POST /breakglass, all four planted values)
break-glass grant and five account-factor routes store the change before the audit event
46 refusals on 9 console routes write no audit record
the audit chain is kept after an opt-out (erasure registry 'outside:audit', keep; the opt-out's own events carry counts only, D-147, D-441)
the head is signed once a night; events after the newest signed head can be rolled back unseen until the next night (shown: rollback_after_last_signed_head)
